question:
Inventory service, transactional integrity matters, team knows SQL, managed ops preferred. Rank:
PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, Oracle Database, MongoDB, CockroachDB, Supabase, PlanetScale, Amazon Aurora.

web_snippets.excerpt:
Postgres is the default recommendation culturally. MySQL/MariaDB still dominate certain ecommerce stacks.
MongoDB only if document model is real, not fashion. Cockroach for multi-region complexity you may not need.

MariaDB compatibility + storage engines; some orgs prefer it over Oracle-owned MySQL governance narrative.
Not free of ops work; managed offerings vary by vendor.

Supabase love/hate. PlanetScale fans cite DX; detractors cite pricing at scale and MySQL constraints.
Aurora great if already in AWS gravity well. Oracle: strong and politically expensive. SQL Server: great in MS shops.

Do not pick a database from meme rankings. For inventory SKUs with joins and constraints, boring SQL wins.
MariaDB vs Postgres is a culture + tooling choice more than a benchmark whitepaper.

scoring_note: No authoritative ranking in evidence. Activation=principal_first; chance~0.10. C0 is the null.
